    Semistability and shrunk subspaces of a projective matrix space #

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.TwoTerm.exists_trace_of_hom_subspace (k : Type u) [Field k] {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (P : TwoTerm R) (M : FGModuleCat R) (U : Submodule k (P.target ⟶ M)) (V : Submodule k (P.source ⟶ M)) (hUV : ∀ (p : P.source ⟶ P.target) (f : ↥U), CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp p ↑f ∈ V) :
    ∃ (T : FGModuleCat R) (i : T ⟶ M), CategoryTheory.Mono i ∧ U ≤ (CategoryTheory.Linear.rightComp k P.target i).range ∧ (CategoryTheory.Linear.rightComp k P.source i).range ≤ V

    For any subspace of maps out of the target projective, take the sum of their images. Every map from the source projective to this sum lifts through a finite sum of target projectives.

    source
    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.TwoTerm.isSemistable_iff_no_shrunk_subspace (k : Type u) [Field k] {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (P : TwoTerm R) (M : FGModuleCat R) :
    (eulerWeight k P).IsSemistable M ↔ homFinrank k P.target M = homFinrank k P.source M ∧ ∀ (U : Submodule k (P.target ⟶ M)) (V : Submodule k (P.source ⟶ M)), (∀ (p : P.source ⟶ P.target) (f : ↥U), CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp p ↑f ∈ V) → Module.finrank k ↥U ≤ Module.finrank k ↥V

    The Hom spaces of a semistable module are balanced, and the full space of projective differentials has no shrunk subspace. These two numerical conditions also imply semistability.

    theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.TwoTerm.strict_expansion_of_stable (k : Type u) [Field k] {R : Type u} [Ring R] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] [IsNoetherianRing R] {P : TwoTerm R} {M : FGModuleCat R} (hs : (eulerWeight k P).IsStable M) (U : Submodule k (P.target ⟶ M)) (V : Submodule k (P.source ⟶ M)) (hne : U ≠ ⊥) (hproper : U ≠ ⊤) (hUV : ∀ (p : P.source ⟶ P.target) (f : ↥U), CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp p ↑f ∈ V) :
    Module.finrank k ↥U < Module.finrank k ↥V

    For a stable module, the image of each proper nonzero Hom subspace under all differentials spans a strictly larger space.
